2024_146_accountability_plan_12_3_24.paragraph: Presented to the Troy School District Board of Education on December 3, 2024, the Accountability Plan slide deck reports progress against the four "World Class for All" pillars: Green (Early Childhood to Career), Red (Equity and Well-Being), Blue (Deep Learning), and Gold (Building Capacity of Students, Staff, and Families). Each pillar is laid out as objectives, December 2024 celebrations and key results, and challenges and recommendations. Among the reported results, GSRP preschool slots increased from 98 to 160, the Career Accelerator Program grew to 60 students, and more than 290 students from the Class of 2024 earned completer status in a Career and Technical Education course.
2024_146_accountability_plan_12_3_24.page:
**Format and purpose**
PowerPoint presentation delivered at the December 3, 2024 Troy School District Board of Education meeting. The framing slide states that the "World Class for All" pillars hold the team accountable to Objectives and Key Results. Each of the four color-coded pillars is presented in the same sequence: objectives, December 2024 celebrations and key results, and challenges and recommendations.

**Green Pillar - Early Childhood to Career**
Objectives: invest in high-quality early childhood education, including advocating for universal preschool for all three- and four-year-olds; expand college and career pathways through high-quality CTE that connects underrepresented students to in-demand careers; and build a consistent K-12 career readiness plan.
Key results: GSRP slots increase from 98 to 160; Portrait of A Learner; K-8 career readiness engagement with Media Specialists and Maker Space; the 99b Computer Science / Computational Thinking Grant; K-12 CS alignment with Oakland Schools and MDE; Early Middle College with LTU; a Business Round Table; Career Accelerator Program increase to 60 students; 8th grade interviews and portfolio integrated with middle school Celebrations of Learning; and Athens named one of two schools in the state to pilot the Ignite Program (Mechatronics). More than 290 students from the class of 2024 earned CTE completer status across eleven listed fields including Mechatronics, Automotive Technician, Computer Programming, Finance, and Woodworking.
Challenges: transition to a 5 Day Model; preparation for universal preschool; the stigma of career readiness; embedding career readiness through building leaders; digital citizenship K-12; growing computer science; and shifting from electives to CTE programs.

**Red Pillar - Equity and Well-Being**
Objectives center on equity and well-being, funding investments for the whole child, an elevated district-wide focus on Alignment, Access, and Agency, and assessing needs for a world class learning environment. Key results: an SEL curriculum pilot and SEL-focused programming K-12; Behavioral Threat Assessment and Suicide Risk Assessment committee work; Belonging Focus Group Sessions and Student Equity Council expansion; the Community Book Read; and all building teams trained in restorative culture as of November 2024. Challenges note over 1600 SEL lessons in Everyday Speech utilized September through November, partnership with Margaret Coggins and the BTA Team, NTAC adoption, and suicide awareness professional learning in Winter 2024.

**Blue Pillar - Deep Learning**
Objectives: MTSS systems of support that empower student voice, improved technology access and training, global best practices (NPDL, The 6 C's, learning partnerships), and upgraded facilities. Slides cover furniture, playgrounds, and student designs and input, noting 36 teachers piloting furniture K-12 alongside student quotations. Curriculum and pedagogy items include full days of professional learning on October 31st and November 1st, implementation of NWEA and Common Lit standardized assessments, pilot work in Geometry, review in Spanish and French, an elementary ELD Newcomer curriculum pilot, and a Grades 11/12 ELA Course Study Team. MTSS work includes partnership with New Solutions K-12 and Solution Tree, a teacher consultant model for Special Education, and an artificial intelligence leadership committee. Challenges: coordinating MTSS across teams, substitute teacher coverage, and systemness.

**Gold Pillar - Building Capacity**
Objectives address educator preparation, pipelines for underrepresented educators, job-embedded professional learning, and co-designed experiences for the OneTroy community. Key results list the Fielding International Partnership, NSK12, Solution Tree, Community Book Read, Learning Nights at all schools, counseling systemness 6-12, website launch feedback sessions, and WEB, LEAP, and the Student Leadership Conference. Challenges include partnership with Celebrate Hope, attracting experienced staff from outside the district, retention strategies, leadership cohorts, and a new teacher learning series.

**Closing**
A "What's Next?" slide quotes that the world's best school systems ensure all stakeholders understand the purpose, priorities, and goals of the system, with leaders clarifying a few very specific non-negotiables while encouraging autonomy and creativity at all levels.
2024_146_accountability_plan_12_3_24.verbose:
Troy School District Accountability Plan presentation delivered to the Board of Education on December 3, 2024, in PowerPoint form. The opening slides identify the district and school (Troy) and establish the framework: the "World Class for All" Pillars hold the team accountable to Objectives and Key Results. The body of the deck walks through four color-coded pillars in turn, each with an objectives slide, a December 2024 celebrations and key results slide, and a challenges and recommendations slide.

GREEN PILLAR - EARLY CHILDHOOD TO CAREER
Objectives: continue to invest in high-quality early childhood education, including advocating for access to universal preschool for all three- and four-year-olds; expand college and career pathways for middle and high school students by offering high-quality career and technical education, with the plan connecting underrepresented students to in-demand careers in high-growth industries through partnerships with colleges, employers, and stakeholders, enabling work-based learning, credential earning, and college credit opportunities; and build a consistent career readiness plan for students K-12.
December 2024 celebrations and key results: an increase in GSRP slots from 98 to 160; consistent priority on percent Preschool Experience Data; Portrait of A Learner; career readiness engagement opportunities K-8 partnered with Media Specialists and Maker Space; the 99b Computer Science / Computational Thinking Grant; K-12 computer science alignment with Oakland Schools and the Michigan Department of Education; expanded maker-centered learning spaces to the high school; continued prioritization of post-secondary learning partnerships throughout K-12; Early Middle College with LTU; a Business Round Table; a Career Accelerator Program increase to 60 students; 8th grade interviews and portfolio integrated with middle school Celebrations of Learning; Athens named as one of two schools in the state to pilot the Ignite Program (Mechatronics); and a process of reviewing and updating CTE programs to make improvements, build stronger connections with business and industry, and provide students the opportunity to earn credentials.
A dedicated slide records that more than 290 students from the class of 2024 earned completer status in one of the district's CTE courses, listing Education, Radio & Television Broadcasting, Marketing, Finance, Drafting & Design Technology, Cooking and Culinary Arts, Automotive Technician, Computer Programming, Mechatronics, Business, and Woodworking.
December 2024 challenges and recommendations: transition to a 5 Day Model; preparation for universal preschool (expanding access); mindshifting the stigma of career readiness to prioritize relevance to learning in classrooms; supporting all building leaders to embed career readiness initiatives in classrooms and beyond; Portrait of a Learner, leveraging and embracing its connection to the current strategic plan; prioritizing digital citizenship for K-12; growing and developing computer science in the K-12 curriculum; and shifting from electives to CTE programs.

RED PILLAR - EQUITY AND WELL-BEING
Objectives: ensuring a focus on equity and well-being; funding additional investments to support the needs of the whole child; an elevated district-wide focus on Alignment, Access, and Agency; and assessing needs and taking action to meet the demands of a world class learning environment in all school communities.
December 2024 celebrations and key results: an SEL curriculum pilot and SEL-focused programming K-12; Behavioral Threat Assessment (BTA) and Suicide Risk Assessment committee work; elevating student experience through Belonging Focus Group Sessions and Student Equity Council expansion; family and community engagement via the Community Book Read and the Continuing the Conversation Series; and restorative culture and community, with all building teams trained as of November 2024.
Challenges and recommendations: community engagement and partnerships with continued intentional collaboration and connection; encouraging and implementing aligned structures; equity teamwork across buildings; SEL curriculum and SEL support/instruction K-12, noting that over 1600 SEL lessons in Everyday Speech were utilized September through November; continued partnership with Margaret Coggins and the BTA Team, including behavioral threat assessment consistency through NTAC adoption, suicide awareness professional learning in Winter 2024, and consistent expectations across all levels and teams; restorative practices including counseling, team, and department fundamentals training, train-the-trainer work to build capacity, and community involvement and awareness; and Belonging as a North Star, continued through an Inclusive Newsletter, professional learning, and student support.

BLUE PILLAR - DEEP LEARNING
Objectives: create and sustain systems of support at all levels that deepen learning and empower student voice (MTSS), with access to deep learning described as imperative for all children; improve technology access for students and families while providing quality training to leverage technology to deepen learning; continue to pursue the global best practices of all content areas (NPDL, The 6 C's, learning partnerships); and assess the need and take action for upgraded facilities to meet the demands of a world-class learning environment in all school communities.
Separate slides are devoted to Furniture, Playgrounds, and Student Designs and Input for Playgrounds and Furniture. The student input slide records 36 teachers piloting furniture K-12 and quotes students: "We need places to climb and play sports to get our energy out!"; "I like rockers because I can rock on them and sit on the carpet to read. It's easy to concentrate and it's comfy."; "My favorite stuff is something I can move with."; and "We want shade and nice places to relax with our friends in nature."
Curriculum and pedagogy: focused attention on Professional Learning Communities at the secondary level; targeted learning on Universal Design and MTSS at the secondary level; continued learning around learning environments in coordination with bond initiatives; development of an Artificial Intelligence leadership committee; development of a Computer Science leadership team; and continuing to grow digital portfolios for students to document learning over time. A second curriculum slide lists October 31st and November 1st as full days of professional learning - elementary on classroom environments and MTSS in mathematics, secondary on universal design, plus choice sessions - along with implementation of NWEA and Common Lit standardized assessments and ongoing development of the MTSS process, and continued curricular work comprising pilot work in Geometry, a review process in Spanish and French, a pilot of the elementary ELD Newcomer curriculum, and a Grades 11/12 ELA Course Study Team.
Multi-Tiered Systems of Support: partnership with New Solutions K-12 and a plan for implementation of its recommendations. Elementary MTSS work continues to monitor benchmark data, develop capacity in math, and solidify tier-one instruction in all classrooms. Secondary MTSS teams meet regularly to support student needs, consider system data to be utilized, build a continuum of services to include a teacher consultant model for Special Education, and partner with Solution Tree to build instructional leadership capacity.
Challenges and recommendations: coordinating MTSS implementation across teams (principals, teachers, content areas, support staff); continuously supporting all content areas; substitute teacher coverage; systemness and building capacity of all staff; and helping staff see connections across content area and level.

GOLD PILLAR - BUILDING CAPACITY OF STUDENTS, STAFF, AND FAMILIES
Objectives: improving educator preparation, strengthening pipelines for underrepresented educators, and supporting current educators; continuing to provide job-embedded professional learning experiences for all staff; and providing professional learning opportunities for staff, community, and students with the goal of co-designing impactful experiences to better the OneTroy community.
Key results: job-embedded learning for staff through the Fielding International Partnership, NSK12, Solution Tree, the Community Book Read, and Learning Nights at all schools; use of early release days to prioritize conversations with collaborative teacher teams around student learning and emerging professional learning communities; building systemness with counseling 6-12 around program opportunities; engaging stakeholders in feedback sessions on the website launch; and building student capacity through WEB, LEAP, and the Student Leadership Conference.
Challenges and recommendations: continued partnership with Celebrate Hope; continued investigation into attracting experienced staff from outside of the district; retention strategies; building community partnerships; continued collaboration among departments within Sub Cabinet; leadership cohorts; and a new teacher learning series.

CLOSING
The final content slide is titled "What's Next?" and carries the quotation: "The world's best school systems ensure that all stakeholders understand the purpose, priorities, and goals of the system. Leaders clarify a few very specific non-negotiables that must be honored throughout the system and at the same time they encourage autonomy and creativity at all levels to foster ownership and innovation."

2024_148_student_achievement_data_review.paragraph: Titled "Exploring Our Data Story," this Troy School District presentation to the Board of Education on November 19, 2024 reviews district goals and walks through summative assessments (M-STEP grades 3-7, PSAT 8, SAT 11, Advanced Placement) and formative classroom assessments (Fountas & Pinnell, Bridges Math, Common Lit, NWEA), plus exit data. The TCCHS four-year graduation rate is charted at 32, 48, 47, 64, 77, and 83 percent for 2019 through 2024, and more than 290 students from the Class of 2024 earned CTE completer status.
2024_148_student_achievement_data_review.page:
**Meeting and objectives**
"Exploring Our Data Story," Board of Education Meeting, November 19, 2024. Objectives: review district goals, provide context to enhance understanding of data, and share how data is utilized to drive systems and processes.

**Assessment inventory**
Summative: M-STEP (Gr 3-7), PSAT 8 / SAT 11, College Board Advanced Placement. Formative: Fountas & Pinnell (K-5), Bridges Math (K-5), Common Lit (ELA 6-12), NWEA Math (6-Alg 1). Exit data includes the TCCHS graduation rate.

**PSAT 8**
| Series | 2018-19 | 2021-22 | 2022-23 | 2023-24 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EBRW - TSD | 87.1 | 81 | 85.6 | 84.2 |
| EBRW - Oakland Schools | 70.3 | 67 | 68.4 | 71.4 |
| EBRW - State | 61.9 | 59.7 | 59.7 | 64.5 |
| Math - TSD | 75.1 | 67.5 | 69 | 64.3 |
| Math - Oakland Schools | 52.5 | 44.6 | 45.5 | 42.3 |
| Math - State | 41.4 | 36.2 | 36.2 | 32.6 |

**SAT 11th grade**
| Series | 2018-19 | 2021-22 | 2022-23 | 2023-24 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EBRW - TSD | 82.9 | 75.3 | 76.9 | 77.3 |
| EBRW - Oakland Schools | 62.9 | 59 | 59.3 | 59.6 |
| EBRW - State | 55.3 | 51.6 | 52.2 | 51.3 |
| Math - TSD | 73.6 | 61.6 | 61.3 | 59.5 |
| Math - Oakland Schools | 46.7 | 39.3 | 38.9 | 35.7 |
| Math - State | 36.3 | 30 | 29.9 | 26.3 |

SAT overall performance, the percent of 11th graders meeting or exceeding expectations in both Math and EBRW, is charted on an axis spanning 2018-19 to 2023-24 with values of 69.8, 58.8, 59.7, and 57 for TSD; 44.5, 37.3, 37.1, and 34.4 for Oakland Schools; and 33.9, 28.1, 28.2, and 25.1 for the State.

**Use of data**
Summative data feeds the MTSS process, collaboration, and ongoing adjustments, plus a partnership with NSK12 to evaluate supports for students with services in ELD, Special Education, and other areas. Areas of focus: access to Tier 1 core instruction for all, access to content-strong staff, and additional time for learning. NWEA is now a universal screener for middle school mathematics, enabling participation in a third-party study with Illustrative Mathematics. Common Lit supports baseline performance, identifying needs, monitoring growth, and goal setting.

**Celebrations**
International Academy East IB Diploma acquisition: 82% (2019), 90% (2020), 87% (2021), 88% (2022), 72% (2023), 81% (2024). AP Honor Roll school overall: Troy High School Gold in 2023-24 and 2022-23; Athens High School Gold in 2023-24 and Silver in 2022-23, with Troy's College Culture at 75% (381/510) in 2023-24. AP 11 ELA enrollment reached 402 of 948 11th graders (42%) in 2024. Seal of Biliteracy recipients: 9 in 2019, 3 in 2021, 3 in 2022, 5 in 2023, 15 in 2024, and 18 marked with an asterisk for 2025. The TCCHS four-year graduation rate is charted at 32, 48, 47, 64, 77, and 83 for 2019 through 2024. More than 290 students from the Class of 2024 earned CTE completer status.

**Next steps**
"Reading Between the Lines" identifies district improvement needs: screening and diagnostics to improve the MTSS process, formation of work groups to build capacity, and shared ownership of the MTSS process. The deck closes with "Sharing Troy's Success Stories."
2024_148_student_achievement_data_review.verbose:
"Exploring Our Data Story" was presented to the Troy School District Board of Education at its meeting of November 19, 2024. The stated objectives were to review district goals, provide context to enhance understanding of data, and share how data is utilized to drive district systems and processes.

ASSESSMENT FRAMEWORK
A slide titled "Beyond the Cover: Understanding Summative & Formative Assessment" organizes the district's measures: building a strong foundation and early childhood enrollment; district-level summative assessments consisting of M-STEP (Gr 3-7), PSAT 8 / SAT 11, and College Board Advanced Placement; classroom-level formative assessments consisting of Fountas & Pinnell (K-5), Bridges Math (K-5), Common Lit (ELA 6-12), and NWEA - Math (6-Alg 1); and exit data, specifically the TCCHS graduation rate.
Under "Snapshots of Progress," the presentation recognizes the limitations of summative M-STEP and PSAT/SAT data: cohort tracking allows monitoring of student cohort performance over time; comparative insights allow assessment against other districts; and granularity issues mean summative data lacks detailed analysis for specific performance insights.

M-STEP
Chart slides are presented for ELA M-STEP Grades 3-7 with county comparison and FRL rate, for M-STEP Math Grades 3-7 with county comparison and FRL rate, and for Middle School M-STEP Grades 6 and 7 covering English Language Arts and Mathematics. The underlying values for these graphics are not carried in the document text.

PSAT 8 RESULTS
The PSAT 8 Evidence-Based Reading & Writing (EBRW) chart plots Troy School District (TSD), Oakland Schools, and the State across 2018-19, 2021-22, 2022-23, and 2023-24. TSD: 87.1, 81, 85.6, 84.2. Oakland Schools: 70.3, 67, 68.4, 71.4. State: 61.9, 59.7, 59.7, 64.5.
The PSAT 8 Math chart, over the same four periods, shows TSD at 75.1, 67.5, 69, and 64.3; Oakland Schools at 52.5, 44.6, 45.5, and 42.3; and the State at 41.4, 36.2, 36.2, and 32.6. A further slide is labeled "2023-24 PSAT 8" and compares the OS LEA Average with TSD.

SAT 11TH GRADE RESULTS
SAT 11th grade Evidence Based Reading & Writing (EBRW) over 2018-19, 2021-22, 2022-23, and 2023-24: TSD 82.9, 75.3, 76.9, 77.3; Oakland Schools 62.9, 59, 59.3, 59.6; State 55.3, 51.6, 52.2, 51.3.
SAT 11th grade Math over the same periods: TSD 73.6, 61.6, 61.3, 59.5; Oakland Schools 46.7, 39.3, 38.9, 35.7; State 36.3, 30, 29.9, 26.3.
SAT Overall Performance, defined as the percent of 11th grade students who meet or exceed expectations in both Math and EBRW, is charted on an axis spanning 2018-19, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23, and 2023-24 with a 0 to 80 scale. Plotted values are 69.8, 58.8, 59.7, and 57 for TSD; 44.5, 37.3, 37.1, and 34.4 for Oakland Schools; and 33.9, 28.1, 28.2, and 25.1 for the State. TSD exceeds both Oakland Schools and the State on every summative measure shown.

REFLECTIONS AND USES OF SUMMATIVE DATA
Summative data informs the MTSS process, collaboration, and ongoing adjustments, along with a partnership with NSK12 to evaluate supports and structure for students with services in ELD, Special Education, and other areas. Areas of focus are access to Tier 1 core instruction for all; access to content-strong staff, framed as who is teaching the content and intervention; additional time for learning, framed as more time with content-strong staff; and ongoing professional learning, with the October 31 and November 1 Trailguide given as an example.

USING DATA TO INFORM INSTRUCTION
Under MTSS Decision Making, "MTSS Time" covers building data and trends; the principle that MTSS is for all children; bringing students with IEPs into scheduling discussions; reviewing progress monitoring of any student on a plan; working on team dynamics; starting with celebrations; and reviewing all data points. Chart slides display the Fountas & Pinnell Benchmark by grade level and a Math Benchmark by grade.
For NWEA mathematics, the district has established a universal screener for middle school mathematics; middle school math specialists use it to identify which students need further, more diagnostic assessment within the MTSS process; and it allows the district to participate in a third-party study with Illustrative Mathematics. A slide addresses NWEA informing classroom-level decisions.
The Common Lit assessment is described in five functions: assessment as a baseline, establishing a starting point for student performance; identifying needs, recognizing students who require immediate support; data-driven instruction, using results to inform whole-class lessons and small group activities; monitoring growth, measuring student progress over time; and goal setting, engaging students in setting personal learning objectives based on assessment results. A sample classroom report from Common Lit is shown.
